The refinement network uses hierarchical sparse 3D convolutional blocks, symmetric encoder-decoder stages, and upsampling layers connected by skip connections [S2].

The claim states that the refinement network uses hierarchical sparse 3D convolutional blocks, symmetric encoder-decoder stages, and upsampling layers connected by skip connections. Source [S2] explicitly states: 'The refinement network is implemented with hierarchical sparse 3D convolutional blocks, symmetric encoder-decoder stages, and upsampling layers connected by skip connections.' This matches the claim exactly.

Use the sparse variant when spatial consistency and structural fidelity need refinement from coarse voxel features [S2].

The claim states that the sparse variant is used when spatial consistency and structural fidelity need refinement from coarse voxel features. The evidence explicitly states: 'To improve the spatial consistency and structural fidelity of the voxel representation, we apply an explicit voxel feature refinement stage... Given an input voxel grid V... a sparse convolutional 3D U-Net R predicts a residual voxel field R... The residual formulation encourages the network to learn correction terms... rather than relearning the entire feature content, which empirically stabilizes training and preserves the coarse voxel information.' This confirms that the sparse 3D U-Net is used for refining spatial consistency and structural fidelity while preserving coarse voxel information.

Voxel-grid Super-Resolution predicts an upsampled voxel grid of higher resolution from a lower-resolution input grid using a U-Net style encoder-decoder network [S1].

The claim states that Voxel-grid Super-Resolution predicts an upsampled voxel grid of higher resolution from a lower-resolution input grid using a U-Net style encoder-decoder network. Predict a residual voxel field $R$ where $R \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times C}$ and $R = R(V)$, with $V$ denoting the set of occupied voxels [S2].

The claim states that the evidence supports predicting a residual voxel field $R$ where $R$ is a function of the set of occupied voxels $V$ ($R = R(V)$). Source [S2] explicitly states in Equation (7) and the surrounding text: 'Given an input voxel grid V... a sparse convolutional 3D U-Net R predicts a residual voxel field R: $R_i ∈ R^{V×C}, R = R(V)$, where V denotes the set of occupied voxels'. This matches the claim exactly.
